newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Southcorp sets 2000 leading profit target.
newsitem.headline: Southcorp sets 2000 leading profit target.

text.p: Wine, packaging and appliance group Southcorp Holdings Ltd said on Friday it aimed to be the world's most profitable wine company by 2000.

"We believe we are the fourth most profitable wine company in the world. By around 2000, we expect to be the most profitable," Southcorp chief executive and managing director Graham Kraehe told a luncheon.
Kraehe said Southcorp saw itself making another step forward to be clearly the leading premium wine producer in the world.
Southcorp saw the international demand for red wine rising by 20 percent a year until at least 2005, he added.
Kraehe said the company was well-positioned to take advantage of this growth and expected high double-digit growth from its wine division in at least the next few years.
Kraehe said Southcorp was looking to supplement that growth with further international wine acquisitions.
He said the aim of these international acquisitions was to to take advantage of a world shortage of red wine and to diversify the company's vintage risk.
"We have very strong growth in-ground but we do want to extend our vintage growth out another two or three years," he said.
Southcorp announced on Friday it had bought a 250-hectare property in California to develop its first offshore vineyard.
The Paso Robles vineyard on the central Californian coast would represent an investment of A$15 million when planting was completed in three years, Southcorp said.
Kraehe said vineyards in the United States were at a premium because of the red wine shortage and the company hoped to gradually build its portfolio in that area rather than pay top prices.
Southcorp Wines is Australia's largest wine producer and the world's eighth largest producer.
The company said it believed it was the world's largest vineyard holder with more than 6,000 hectares of vineyards in Australia.
